Run a chat app, connect it to a model, then try the other UI styles and layouts.

Scaffold a starter app for any framework (agent, openai, anthropic, langgraph, crewai, pydantic-ai, praisonai, or dashboard): Or create app.py directly: Run it: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 and send a message. If port 8000 is taken, aiui run picks the next free port and prints the URL it used. aiui run app.py opens in the React app shell (style: app) in focused mode (Chat + your own pages). Pass --preset agent to add Sessions, Approvals, Usage and Memory, or --preset ops for the full control plane. The minimal example is examples/python/01-chat.

Stream tokens from any client library with aiui.stream_token(). With OpenAI (pip install openai), set your key first: Then open a new terminal. aiui run also reads a .env file in the current folder (and ~/.praisonai/.env) without overriding variables already set. examples/python/03-chat-with-ai adds conversation history, a welcome message and starters.
The app shell has selectable layouts. Pick one per run with AIUI_LAYOUT, or in the app with aiui.set_layout(): See React app shell and Layouts for every layout.

Register a custom page with @aiui.page — or wrap any Python function (including yield generators) with aiui.interface(). An app with pages opens in the React app shell (style: app) in focused mode (Chat + your own pages); pass --preset ops for all built-in ops views, or --style dashboard for the legacy vanilla dashboard: How the style is chosen: --style on the command line wins, then aiui.set_style() in the app. Without either, aiui run opens the React app shell (app), or agents when @aiui.profiles is paired with registered agents. See UI Styles and Build a focused app.
A YAML file can define the agent without Python. It runs on PraisonAI Agents, so install that first: pip install praisonaiagents (or the full pip install "aiui[praisonai]"), and set OPENAI_API_KEY.
aiui build turns a folder of Markdown into a static site: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs/. To publish it, see Deploy to GitHub Pages.
